article_notes: Longitudinal field study of owned free-roaming dogs (Zenzele, South Africa) from a rabies-control study. The only severity contrast is a narrative case description of 18 smear-positive dogs (fatal vs mild vs subclinical); per-dog data are in Supplementary Table S4, not in the text. Serology results (IFAT seropositive dogs consistently healthy) are not compared against an outcome group. B. rossi confirmed by PCR-RLB in 13 of 15 tested dogs; 3 dogs smear-only.

severity_definitions.label: fatal babesiosis (confirmed or suspected) vs subclinical infection or mild disease
severity_definitions.definition: Among 18 community dogs positive for Babesia spp. on blood smear (13 confirmed B. rossi by PCR-RLB), fatal babesiosis was confirmed in one juvenile and suspected in one juvenile and one probably very old adult; the other dogs had transient mild disease (3 adults) or no or non-specific clinical signs (9 adults, 3 juveniles). Case-series description; no statistical comparison.
severity_definitions.comparison_group: mild disease (n=3) or subclinical / non-specific signs (n=12)
severity_definitions.quote: Fatal babesiosis was confirmed in one juvenile (dog 10) and suspected in one other juvenile (dog 15) and one (probably) very old

associations.statistic: fatal: 2 juveniles and 1 (probably) very old adult; mild disease: 3 adults; no or non-specific signs: nine adults and three juveniles
associations.quote: Fatal babesiosis was confirmed in one juvenile (dog 10) and suspected in one other juvenile (dog 15) and one (probably) very old
associations.note: Descriptive case series. The comparison group is the other 15 smear-positive dogs (3 adults with mild disease; 9 adults and 3 juveniles with no or non-specific signs, Results 3.2). Authors note in the Discussion that fatal babesiosis was suspected only in young juveniles and possibly a very old dog. No test.
